data.text: During his time in Rome, Paul continued coaching and mentoring believers in Philippi, Colossae and Ephesus through letter writing. Paul also wrote a personal letter to a church leader in Colossae named Philemon. This letter reveals that Paul anticipated being released ({Philemon 1:22}).

references.label: Philemon 1:22
references.passage: 22 And one thing more: Prepare a guest room for me, because I hope to be restored to you in answer to your prayers.

data.text: Church history shows us that Paul was indeed released from prison and did more missionary travel ({Titus 3:12},

references.label: Titus 3:12
references.passage: 12 As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.

references.label: 2 Timothy 4:20
references.passage: 20 Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.

data.text: He continued church planting and wrote three more personal letters to leaders he had developed.
Paul and Peter are both killed around 67 AD after their second letters are written around:
